simple_description: A persistent daily headache caused by frequent, regular use of acute pain relievers or migraine medications for headaches, creating a vicious cycle of rebound pain.
medical_description: Headache occurring on 15 or more days per month in a patient with a pre-existing primary headache disorder, developing as a consequence of regular overuse of acute or symptomatic headache medication (>= 10 days/month for triptans, opioids, or combination analgesics; or >= 15 days/month for simple analgesics) for more than 3 months.
affected_system: Central pain modulation, descending serotonergic pathways, and trigeminal sensitization.
symptoms: Daily or near-daily dull, throbbing, or mixed-character headache present upon waking
Headache temporarily improves with painkillers, only to return worse as the dose wears off
Gradual increase in medication consumption over months
Associated restlessness, anxiety, asthenia, and poor sleep quality
early_warning_signs: Needing painkiller tablets more than 2 to 3 days every single week
possible_causes: Receptor down-regulation and central sensitization caused by repetitive intermittent drug exposure
Alterations in endocannabinoid and endogenous opioid systems
risk_factors: Use of combination analgesics containing caffeine, codeine, or butalbital
High psychological stress and sleep disturbance
clinical_evaluation: Detailed chronological drug diary showing frequency, dose, and days per month of all prescription and over-the-counter pain medications.
diagnostic_tests: Rule out secondary structural etiologies with Brain MRI if atypical features exist
treatment_overview: Structured withdrawal of the overused acute medication under neurological guidance, initiation of effective preventive therapy (e.g. Topiramate, Amitriptyline, or CGRP monoclonal antibodies), and patient education.
medication_classes: Preventive bridging: Corticosteroid taper (Prednisone 60 mg tapered over 10 days) or Greater Occipital Nerve block during withdrawal
Maintenance prevention: Topiramate, OnabotulinumtoxinA, CGRP mAbs (Erenumab, Fremanezumab)
Non-overused rescue alternatives (limited strictly to <= 2 days/week)
precautions: Do NOT increase analgesic doses when headaches become more frequent; it perpetuates the cycle
Strict limit on acute headache medications to no more than 2 days per week
prevention: Start non-analgesic preventive medication early if headaches occur > 4 days/month
Avoid multi-ingredient analgesics containing caffeine and codeine
complications: Gastric ulceration or renal impairment from chronic NSAID overuse
emergency_signs: Severe withdrawal symptoms including seizures or acute delirium (especially with butalbital or opioid withdrawal)

faqs.question: Can regular painkillers actually cause more headaches?
faqs.answer: Yes. When taken more than 10 to 15 days a month, pain relievers reset the brain's pain threshold, causing a rebound headache every time the drug wears off.

hi.name: दवा के अधिक उपयोग से सिरदर्द (Medication-overuse headache)
hi.summary: पेनकिलर या माइग्रेन की दवाएं बहुत ज्यादा लेने से होने वाला रोजाना का रिबाउंड सिरदर्द।
hi.advice: दवा का सेवन खुद से न बढ़ाएं। न्यूरोलॉजिस्ट की देखरेख में पेनकिलर कम करके प्रिवेंटिव दवा शुरू करें।

hinglish.name: Medication Overuse Headache (Rebound sar dard)
hinglish.summary: Roz-roz painkiller khane se dimaag aadi ho jata hai aur dava ka asar khatam hote hi dobara dard shuru ho jata hai.
hinglish.advice: Painkillers band karein aur doctor se preventive treatment lein.
